findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

During the inspection all of the sanitizer buckets were observed to not register quaternary ammonia sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips. These buckets were observed changed during the inspection and prior to observation. The inspector then checked the dispenser in the kitchen and did not find evidence of the dispenser correctly dispensing sanitizer on either their test strips or the facility test strips. The PIC was consulted at that point and more investigation conducted. The buckets were remade manually with the concentrate and a call will be put in to the company contracted to manage the dispenser (EcoLab) and maintenance will need to be conducted moving forward.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. 

The dispenser used for sanitizers in the facility was not producing sanitizer at effective concentrations for sanitizing food contact surfaces. A temporary fix was put into place until EcoLab could be contacted and conduct maintenance. A ten day follow-up is being scheduled to allow for this maintenance to be completed.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

Multiple shelves above the three part sink have the paint worn away and chipping. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and re-seal prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all surfaces subject to moisture are smooth and easily cleanable at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

Heavy ice accumulation is observed in the walk in freezer. Previously this violation was noted as on the floor only and now includes major frost accumulation around the unit and ceiling of the freezer. The PIC is instructed to clean/defrost the area regularly to ensure an accumulation does not develop again. It is also suggested to have a professional examine the equipment and see if there is an external reason for the accumulation to develop.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival the sani buckets were all registering low on the inspector’s test strips. The buckets were remade during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

The thermometer in the reach in cooler next to the drive thru window has mold accumulation along the seams and back surface. Clean and maintain clean moving forward.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Multiple wiping rags used for cleaning spills off the counters are observed moist and sitting on the counters in the service area. Both flat sani buckets are also observed with heavily soiled solutions. The PIC was consulted, buckets remade with clean solution and the rags placed in solution to correct today’s violations.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

During this inspection the PIC was not aware of any equipment in the facility intended for ensuring that the temperature based dish machine reaches the critical temperature of 160F. Strips and dots that change color at 160 were discussed as well as a thermometer intended for measuring dish machines. Ensure that a measuring system is in place prior to the follow up in two weeks.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

The bottom of the walk in freezer is coated with ice during this inspection. The PIC was consulted and instructed to remove the ice often enough to ensure that effective cleaning takes place.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The baffles and internal roof of the ice machine have an accumulation of potential molds built up on their surfaces. A conversation took place with the PIC and they’re instructed to clean these surfaces often enough to maintain them clean. The items were cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Accumulation of soil observed under espresso machines and other counter equipment. Clean frequently enough to prevent soil accumulation. Follow up at next routine inspection.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: No certified food manager (CFM) present during the inspection. Medium risk facilities must have a CFM present at all times of food prep and service.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12 (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. (C)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed egg sandwiches on the left side/top shelf of the food under-counter cooler to be 55F (probed). Items were placed in this cooler at 12PM. Discussed Time as a Public Health Control and the 6 hour time limit on food stored below 70F. CORRECTED- PIC will check temperatures in 1 hour, if still out of temperature, items will be disposed of. Cooler thermometer was relocated to the warmer side of the cooler to aid in temperature monitoring.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16 (A)(2) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained at 5ºC (41ºF) or less. (P)
